summary: Recent updates to Firefox's connection transport mechanics, particularly around ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment) and DTLS (Datagram Transport Layer Security), enhance how the browser handles real-time communications, such as video calls. The changes include improvements to the way the browser reads and processes message IDs from STUN (Session Traversal Utilities for NAT), which helps in establishing connections behind routers. Additionally, new statistics for certificates used in secure connections were introduced, allowing better tracking of security and connection health by implementing RTCCertificateStats and packet metrics. **This means users can expect more reliable connections and enhanced security while using WebRTC, the technology behind video calls.** Overall, these adjustments improve the robustness and efficiency of real-time data transport in Firefox.
